body:
> My main motivation for this change is that in the C# bindings we pass a `null` pointer when calling void-returning methods, I don't really care about discarding the return for non-void-returning methods.

Just conceptually, it seems that this should:

1. not be a runtime check, but something known statically based on the method
2. be determined by the GDExtension API itself and not the caller

It's nice to avoid the `Variant` construction though, and I see the compat side as well. Just not sure if it should be done based on the pointer :thinking: 

I assume this change is done for performance reasons, but for situations where a return type _is_ needed, can the `if` statement be branch-predicted reliably enough to not have pessimization for a large number of FFI calls?

Personally, I could go either way on this.

It does sort of make sense for the caller to decide if the return value should be set or not, because, in theory, the caller should know if the return value is going to be used or not. Even if the method isn't void and has a return value, the caller may be aware that it's going to be discarded, so why allocate more memory?

(In practice, the caller probably doesn't actually know, since the GDExtension interface is usually called by language bindings which are always going to capture the return value if the method has one, and the bindings don't know whether the upstream code will use it or not. Maybe in a theoretical godot-c, it would be possible to take advantage of this :-))

I don't really know the performance implications of this change, I guess, someone should do some quick profiling. Although, I expect it to be a wash (especially if the extra `Variant` constructions can be avoid, per my code comment below.)

> It's nice to avoid the `Variant` construction though

This doesn't avoid it at a low level: the `Variant` will still be constructed, it's just whether it'll be constructed into a temporary that is discarded, or into memory provided by the caller. Although, at an API level, it avoids the caller needing to set aside the memory to construct into

So, unless someone can show a performance advantage in one way or another, I think this is purely an API question. And I do think allowing the developer to pass null when they aren't going to use the return is a slightly more friendly API

> (In practice, the caller probably doesn't actually know, since the GDExtension interface is usually called by language bindings which are always going to capture the return value if the method has one, and the bindings don't know whether the upstream code will use it or not

I strongly agree with what @dsnopek says here

On top of that, the only gain I see here is to have the language binding code avoid reserving some space on the stack and passing a pointer when it knows the function doesn't return anything.

However stack reservation is basically free, and the unused variant object is most likely going to be constructed anyway somewhere in the `callp` code (and this construction is very cheap since it's a NIL variant which is basically equivalent to zero-initializing)

And the theoretical performance gains might be balanced out by the runtime `if (r_return != nullptr)` conditional jump...

So I would say this is not worth it.
And if we consider skipping return value for void-returning function is a valid concern (typically we have benchmark showing very common methods have this pattern an benefit from it), then we should provide dedicated methods (e.g. `gdextension_variant_call_no_return(p_method, p_args, p_argcount, r_error)`) so that we can avoid the runtime check and allow further optimization (but I'm doubtful this is needed, especially since it would also require specialized such as `Variant::callp_no_return` to ensure the return value is not constructed somewhere in the call stack...).
Looks like it's not worth it. Thanks for the reviews anyway.
